title: Hamlet
synopsis: Elsinore, winter. Your father is dead. Your uncle is on the throne and in your mother's bed. A ghost is on the battlement and wants a word.

nodes.text: Horatio brings you to see the ghost.

choices.consequence: The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Brave.
The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Wise.

nodes.text: Murdered by Claudius. Revenge me.

choices.consequence: The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Path—follows you into whatever comes next.
You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Wise.

nodes.text: You play mad to buy time.

choices.consequence: You commit to “Play it well.” The story records the instinct as “Cunning” and carries it forward.
You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Honest.

nodes.text: You are cruel to her in the gallery.

choices.consequence: There is no taking “Apologize later” back. Honor shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.
“Don't apologize” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Cold.

nodes.text: He hides behind tapestries to spy.

choices.consequence: There is no taking “Sense him there” back. Wise shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.
You commit to “Walk past.” The story records the instinct as “Honest” and carries it forward.

nodes.text: A troupe arrives. You write them new lines.

choices.consequence: You commit to “Test the king.” The story records the instinct as “Cunning” and carries it forward.
You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Foolish.

nodes.text: Claudius rises and walks out, pale.

choices.consequence: You commit to “Mark his guilt.” The story records the instinct as “Wise” and carries it forward.
There is no taking “Tell only Horatio” back. Smart shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

nodes.text: You find Claudius praying.

choices.consequence: The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Path—follows you into whatever comes next.
You commit to “Wait.” The story records the instinct as “Pride” and carries it forward.

nodes.text: You confront Gertrude. A noise behind the arras.

choices.consequence: You commit to “Stab.” The story records the instinct as “Anger” and carries it forward.

nodes.text: It was Polonius. Ophelia's father.

choices.consequence: There is no taking “Mourn” back. Honor shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.
The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Cold.

nodes.text: Rosencrantz and Guildenstern carry sealed orders.

choices.consequence: The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Cunning.
There is no taking “Trust the friends” back. Naive shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

nodes.text: A skirmish. You return alone.

choices.consequence: You commit to “Send word ahead.” The story records the instinct as “Smart” and carries it forward.
There is no taking “Surprise the court” back. Brave shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

nodes.text: A gravedigger holds a skull.

choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Honor.
“Move on” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Honest.

nodes.text: She is in the ground. Laertes leaps in.

choices.consequence: “Leap in too” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Heart.
The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Wise—follows you into whatever comes next.

nodes.text: He sharpens a foil. He dips it in poison.

choices.consequence: The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Wise—follows you into whatever comes next.
There is no taking “Trust the duel” back. Naive shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

nodes.text: A foolish courtier brings the challenge.

choices.consequence: The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Wit.

nodes.text: Touch. Touch. A scratch with the wrong foil.

choices.consequence: “Switch” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Wise.
The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Honest.

nodes.text: Your mother drinks from the poisoned cup.

choices.consequence: There is no taking “Stop her” back. Mother shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

nodes.text: You finally do it.

choices.text: Pour the cup down his throat
choices.consequence: There is no taking “Pour the cup down his throat” back. Path shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.
There is no taking “Just the blade” back. Honor shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

nodes.text: Horatio raises the cup. You stop him.

choices.consequence: You commit to “Hold him.” The story records the instinct as “Honor” and carries it forward.
You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Honest.

nodes.text: He arrives. He takes the kingdom. Horatio begins to speak.

choices.consequence: The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Honor—follows you into whatever comes next.
“Have him spare the worst” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Civil.
Some endings reveal themselves last.

nodes.text: You die, peacefully enough, with Horatio's hand on your shoulder. The kingdom passes to a foreigner. The story passes to a friend.
You survive, somehow, the scratch. You abdicate. You go to Wittenberg as a tutor. You write down, with Horatio, the play exactly. It survives every revision.
Horatio tells the story. He tells it carefully. He tells it for as long as he lives. The court that came after, slowly, hears it true.
